claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course?** 

(Child Benefit typically continues until a child turns 16, but can be extended up to age 20 if they remain in qualifying education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not. He finished school and he's not studying anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 17 and has finished school without continuing in full-time education or approved training, I need to check one more thing:

**Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks), or has it been longer than that?**

This is relevant because there can sometimes be an extension period after leaving education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been longer than that. He left school a while back now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me just check one more thing:

**Is Alex registered with a careers service or similar organisation (such as Connexions in England) and considered as someone who is not yet in employment but receiving education or training?**

This is sometimes referred to as the "child extension period" for young people who have left education but are registered for training or work.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not registered with anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the rules to make sure I give you an accurate answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the official eligibility rules, I now have enough to make a determination.

Here's the situation for Alex:
- He is 17 years old
- He has left school and is not in full-time education or approved training
- It has been more than 20 weeks since he left education
- He is not registered with a careers service or similar organisation

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Child Benefit for children aged 16 or over** is only available if they remain in approved full-time education or training (until they turn 20).
- There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** after a 16 or 17-year-old leaves education, but only if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Since Alex hasn't done this and it's been longer than 20 weeks since he left school, this option is no longer available.
- Since Alex is 17, has left education, is not in training, and is not registered with a careers service, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. If Alex's circumstances change—for example, if he returns to approved education or training—you may be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point.

If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.

Additionally, there is a provision allowing Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services - however, Alex has not done this and it has been longer than 20 weeks since he left education. Therefore, Alex does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
